papers.abstract_en: IMPORTANCE: Effective interventions are needed to support the cocreation of diabetes care plans that are sensible, desirable, and feasible for the people living with diabetes (ie, care that fits). OBJECTIVE: To investigate whether an agenda-setting kit (ASK) added to usual primary care improves fit of care and glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes (T2D). DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This single-center, clinician-level cluster randomized clinical trial was conducted from February 16, 2023, to July 26, 2024, with a 6-month follow-up, at a federally qualified health center in New Haven, Connecticut. Eligible clinicians were primary care physicians, nurse practitioners, and physician assistants who prescribed medication to treat patients with T2D. Eligible patients were English- or Spanish-speaking adults aged 18 years or older with T2D and hemoglobin (Hb) A1c level greater than 8%. Patients were excluded if their clinician determined that an HbA1c level 8% or lower was inconsistent with goals of care. Data were analyzed from November 7, 2024, to August 13, 2026. INTERVENTION: Clinicians were randomized 1:1 to the ASK plus usual primary care group (intervention group) or usual primary care only (control group). The ASK intervention consisted of 14 conversation cards about life with diabetes and its treatment. Prior to the clinical encounter, patients were asked to select 0 to 3 cards they wanted to prioritize for discussion. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was the 6-month change from baseline in illness intrusiveness measured with the Illness Intrusiveness Ratings Scale (IIRS; range: 13-91, with higher scores indicating greater intrusiveness) and HbA1c level. Secondary outcomes included changes in treatment burden measured with the Treatment Burden Questionnaire (TBQ; range: 0-150, with higher scores indicating greater burden), diabetes distress measured with the 17-Item Diabetes Distress Scale (DDS-17; scores: indicate little or no distress [<2.0], moderate distress [2.0-2.9], and high distress [≥3.0]), and visit satisfaction. RESULTS: Eleven clinicians (6 [54.5%] female) were included in the trial along with 143 of their patients. The mean (SD) patient age was 56 (12) years; 87 participants (60.8%) were female and 88 (61.5%) reported Spanish as their primary language. Six-month survey data were available for 65 of 74 patients (87.8%) in the intervention group and 58 of 69 (84.0%) in the control group; data on HbA1c level were available for 71 (95.9%) and 65 (94.2%), respectively. At 6 months, mean (SD) IIRS scores were 32.1 (15.1) and 37.1 (18.7) in the intervention and control groups (adjusted mean difference, -3.9; 95% CI, -10.4 to 2.6). The mean (SD) HbA1c levels were 8.8% (1.8) in the intervention group and 9.1% (1.8) in the control group (adjusted mean difference, -0.2%; 95% CI, -0.9% to 0.5%). Mean (SD) TBQ scores in the intervention and control groups were 41.2 (44.8) and 46.8 (44.4) (adjusted mean difference, 1.0; 95% CI, -16.6 to 18.6), and mean (SD) DDS-17 scores were 2.0 (1.0) and 2.3 (1.0) (adjusted mean difference, -0.1; 95% CI, -0.4 to 0.2). Clinician-reported satisfaction was greater in the intervention group; patient satisfaction did not differ between groups. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cluster randomized clinical trial of adults with T2D, use of the ASK with usual primary care was associated with greater clinician satisfaction but not with improvements in patients' fit of care or glycemic control over 6 months. Larger studies should evaluate interventions that not only identify patients' priorities and treatment burdens but also better support clinicians in addressing them. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05553912.

Outcomes were assessed at baseline, 6 weeks, 8 weeks (posttreatment), and 3 months (follow-up) by masked evaluators. INTERVENTIONS: Patients were randomized to B4DT (including preparatory sessions) or an 8-week unguided iCBT program. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was the change in OCD symptom severity, measured by the Yale-Brown Obsessive Compulsive Scale (Y-BOCS). Secondary outcomes included self-reported OCD (OCI-R), dysfunctional cognitions, quality of life, depressive symptoms, experiential avoidance, global functioning, self-esteem, and treatment satisfaction. papers.abstract_en: IMPORTANCE: Transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) has emerged as a home-based treatment in major depressive disorder (MDD), although its effects are typically small to moderate and inconsistently observed. Because tDCS may act synergistically with behavioral interventions, combining both approaches represents a promising strategy for developing more effective home-based treatments for MDD. OBJECTIVE: To investigate the feasibility, safety, and efficacy of home-based tDCS and concurrent gamified cognitive control training (CCT) in adults with MDD. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This multicenter, double-masked, parallel-group, randomized clinical trial with follow-up at week 10, masking checks at 2 time points, and expectancy assessments was conducted at 3 university hospitals in Latvia, Germany, and Israel between June 22, 2021, and August 8, 2024. Participants included adults aged 18 to 65 years with MDD, 17-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale scores of at least 13, and no or stable antidepressant medication. INTERVENTION: Participants were randomly assigned 1:1 to active tDCS (2 mA; anode F3, cathode F4) plus a gamified CCT or sham tDCS plus a sham game. Participants were asked to complete 30 home treatment sessions (30 minutes each) over 6 weeks with software-assisted electrode positioning. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was feasibility, defined as completing at least 20 of 30 sessions with greater than 50% probability. The secondary outcome was efficacy, measured as change in Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS) scores from baseline to week 6. RESULTS: Of 111 enrolled participants, 109 were included in the modified intention-to-treat sample (55 in the active group and 54 in the control group; mean [SD] age, 33.1 [10.6] years; 69 female [63.3%]). Feasibility criteria were met, with 86 participants (78.9%) completing at least 20 sessions (lower bound of 1-sided 95% CI, 71.5%). The MADRS scores improved significantly in both groups at week 6, indicating insufficient evidence to reject the null hypothesis of no difference in the mean change in MADRS score from baseline to 6 weeks between the 2 treatment groups (difference, 0.89 [95% CI, -1.37 to 3.15]; P = .44; Cohen d, 0.10 [95% CI, -0.15 to 0.34]). Results were similar at follow-up (week 10). Adverse events were balanced between groups. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This RCT of home-based tDCS combined with CCT in adults with MDD was feasible and safe but did not demonstrate superior efficacy over the control condition. Future studies should refine the mechanistic alignment between stimulation and cognitive interventions to optimize treatment effects. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04953208.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified numerous lung cancer susceptibility loci based on single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), yet a substantial proportion of heritability remains unexplained. We therefore evaluated germline copy number variants (CNVs) as an underexplored source of genetic susceptibility and potential contributors to genomic instability in lung cancer. METHODS: We conducted a genome-wide analysis of germline CNVs using 19,342 cases and 15,917 controls from the Transdisciplinary Research in Cancer of the Lung (TRICL) consortium, with replication in two independent cohorts. High-confidence CNVs were identified by integrating two CNV callers including PennCNV and modSaRa2. Association analyses were performed using both gene-based and CNV region-based approaches. Polygenic risk scores (PRS) were constructed from top loci, and functional validation was conducted using siRNA-mediated knockdown in lung fibroblast cells. RESULTS: We identified CNVs in four genomic regions (1p36.22, 2q31.2, 6p21.32, and 19q13.32) significantly or suggestively associated with lung cancer risk. Two loci (1p36.22 and 2q31.2) were consistently supported across both analytical strategies. A CNV-based PRS constructed from four key genes (CLCN6, NFE2L2, OPA3, and PSMB8) was significantly associated with lung cancer risk and replicated across independent datasets. Functional assays demonstrated that knockdown of NFE2L2 and OPA3 increased endogenous DNA damage, supporting a role in genomic stability. CONCLUSIONS: Germline CNVs contribute to lung cancer susceptibility and may influence carcinogenesis through mechanisms related to genomic instability. IMPACT: These findings expand our knowledge of the genetic architecture of lung cancer and suggest that the cumulative burden of germline CNVs may contribute to lung cancer susceptibility.

papers.abstract_en: Malignant ascites provides a window into cancer-immune interactions in the peritoneal cavity. Using Cytometry by Time of Flight (CyTOF), we analyzed ascitic immune cells collected from patients with advanced gastrointestinal cancers, nonmalignant forms of hepatitis (NMH), and healthy control peripheral blood mononuclear cells (HC PBMCs). Compositionally, ascitic immune cells shared a myeloid-rich, B and naïve T cell-low signature relative to HC PBMCs. Underneath the shared ascitic compositional signature, three major functional immunophenotypes emerged in response to exogenous stimulation along a suppressive to cytotoxic axis, aligning with Luminex measurements of ascitic cytokine levels: IL-10 enriched, Nonpolarized, and Granzyme B (GZMB) enriched. In our cohort, the IL-10 enriched functional immunophenotype was exclusive to samples from patients with cancer while the GZMB enriched response was dominated by NMH samples. Ascites from patients with pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) contained a persistent anti-cancer humoral response characterized by IgG that bound to autologous ascitic PDAC cells and multiple allogeneic PDAC cell lines.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Streptozotocin (STZ)-based chemotherapy remains a treatment option for advanced pancreatic neuroendocrine tumours (PanNETs), particularly when tumour shrinkage is a therapeutic priority. However, its activity has been reported across heterogeneous treatment schedules, patient populations, and response-assessment eras. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to estimate objective response rate (ORR) and landmark progression-free survival (PFS). METHODS: We systematically reviewed randomised trials, prospective studies, and retrospective cohorts reporting ORR and/or PFS with STZ-containing regimens. Random-effects meta-analyses were conducted in a primary ELIGIBLE dataset restricted to advanced or metastatic pancreatic-only cohorts with standardised outcome assessment, and in a broader ALL dataset for contextual analyses. Comparisons across regimen families were exploratory. RESULTS: Twenty-seven studies including 1,744 patients were included. In the ELIGIBLE dataset, pooled ORR was 36.1% (95% CI 30.6-42.0), with a 95% prediction interval of 23.0-51.0%. Landmark PFS was 59.2% (50.6-67.2) at 12 months and 41.5% (33.4-50.1) at 24 months. Estimates from the ALL dataset were directionally consistent but more heterogeneous. No statistically significant differences were detected between regimen families. Certainty of evidence was very low, mainly because of risk of bias and inconsistency. CONCLUSION: In cohorts using standardised outcome assessment, STZ-containing regimens were associated with objective responses in approximately one-third of patients, supporting their consideration when tumour shrinkage is a major therapeutic objective. These single-arm pooled estimates do not establish superiority among STZ schedules or relative to other treatments, and the PFS benchmarks require cautious interpretation because of substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity.

papers.abstract_en: Protein aggregation is a critical phenomenon associated with numerous neurodegenerative and systemic diseases. Understanding the propensity of proteins to aggregate is essential for unraveling the molecular basis of these disorders and for the design and engineering of novel proteins, as well as for modulating the activity/stability of enzymatic proteins. Here, we present APR-Score, a novel machine learning-based computational method designed to identify aggregation-prone regions within protein sequences. APR-Score leverages a combination of sequence-based features to predict regions of proteins that are prone to aggregation. It harnessed the information embedded in compiled sequence and structural features to achieve state-of-the-art accuracy. The method was evaluated through rigorous cross-validation on the training dataset and further validated on an independent test dataset. APR-Score demonstrated robustness and reliability in distinguishing aggregation-prone regions from non-aggregating ones, achieving a Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) of 0.77, precision of 0.89, and F1-Score of 0.87. This tool offers significant value for researchers investigating protein aggregation-related diseases, as it can expedite the identification of aggregation-prone regions, thereby aiding the development of targeted therapies and diagnostic tools. Moreover, computational protein design and engineering efforts can be facilitated by APR-Score-based identification and screening of aggregation-prone protein sequences. APR-Score is available at https://github.com/TII-BRC/APR-Score.

papers.abstract_en: AIMS: High-grade B-cell lymphoma with 11q aberration is a rare neoplasm of mature B-cell lineage, and large-scale clinicopathological studies of this disease remain scarce. To bridge this research gap, we conducted a retrospective analysis of HGBCL with 11q aberration, aiming to elucidate its pathogenesis, clinicopathological features and molecular profiles. METHODS AND RESULTS: By reviewing our hospital's case database from 2021 to 2025, we retrospectively screened 92 cases of high-grade or diffuse large B-cell lymphoma that had 11q fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) testing. Among them, 27 cases were confirmed to harbour 11q aberration and were enrolled in the present study. This cohort consisted of 24 males and 3 females with a median age of 61 years (range, 6-85). Eighteen (67%) patients presented with extranodal disease and nine (33%) had nodal disease. The gastrointestinal tract was the most commonly involved extranodal site (13 patients); two of these patients had concurrent lymph node involvement in the head and neck. Fourteen (52%) patients had advanced Ann Arbor stage (III, IV) disease. Eight (30%) patients had a history of immunocompromise including HIV infection, liver or kidney transplantation and other malignant tumours. The bone marrow was negative for lymphoma at initial diagnosis in all 21 patients assessed. Histologically, 20 (74%) cases had Burkitt-like or blastoid morphology and seven (26%) cases showed diffuse large B-cell-like morphology. Most cases (96%, 26/27) had a germinal centre B-cell immunophenotype. c-MYC was positive in all 26 tested cases and BCL2 was negative in 24 of 27 (89%) of cases. Mutational analysis was performed in 14 cases and potential driver mutations were identified in all involving 44 genes. The most frequently affected genes included TP53, IGLL5, DDX3X, BTG2, FOXO1, HIST1H1E and MYC. Following therapy, 24 patients achieved complete remission and disease-free survival. The prognosis was not related to the morphological features, Ann Arbor stage, co-occurrence of MYC aberrations or the chemotherapy regimens. CONCLUSIONS: High-grade B-cell lymphoma with 11q aberration may occur across all ages and confers a favourable prognosis. These tumours manifest morphological heterogeneity, and most cases display a Burkitt lymphoma-like immunophenotype characterized by CD10 positivity and BCL2 negativity. The most frequently mutated genes in our cohort are TP53, IGLL5, DDX3X, BTG2, FOXO1, HIST1H1E and MYC.

papers.abstract_en: IMPORTANCE: Cancer drug shortages require health systems to rapidly develop and enact allocation policies, yet little is known about how such policies perform in practice. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate clinical implementation of a formal allocation policy during the 2023 carboplatin shortage. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This cohort study comprised a carboplatin shortage at a 7-site health system in Massachusetts and New Hampshire that lasted from June 1 to July 17, 2023. Patients with cancer who were eligible for carboplatin during the shortage were assigned priority categories using predetermined criteria based on treatment intent, inferior or contraindicated alternative treatments, clinical trial participation, and ongoing vs new treatment; these categories were assigned collectively by clinical groups and disease-specific pharmacists after a training session. A structured process conducted between September and November 2025 was used to review medical records and independently reassign categories post hoc. EXPOSURE: Allocation of carboplatin during the shortage vs mandate to switch to an alternative treatment. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Main outcomes were concordance between actual and review-based priority category assignments, actual allocation, and independent review-based allocation, as well as associations of demographic and clinical variables with allocation. Descriptive statistics and multivariable logistic regression assessed actual and review-based outcomes. RESULTS: Allocation decisions were made for 483 patients (median age, 66 years [IQR, 58-73 years]; 354 women [73%]). A total of 222 patients (46%) were allocated carboplatin and 261 (54%) were not. An independent review agreed with 56% of priority category assignments (189 of 335) and 74% of allocation decisions (357 of 483); 26% of allocation decisions (126 of 483) were not aligned with policy intent. Incomplete documentation (51% [74 of 146]) and treatment contraindication discrepancies (21% [31 of 146]) were the most common causes of disagreement. In multivariable regression, male gender (vs female gender; odds ratio [OR], 2.72 [95% CI, 1.26-5.99]; P = .01) and treatment at main campus (vs regional campuses; OR, 2.13 [95% CI, 1.30-3.45]; P < .001) were associated with increased likelihood of receiving carboplatin. In models of policy-concordant allocation based on independent review, these associations were not significant (male gender: OR, 1.39 [95% CI, 0.16-13.08]; P = .77; treatment at main campus: OR, 1.47 [95% CI, 0.33-7.14]; P = .61). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cohort study of allocation policy implementation during a chemotherapy shortage, most allocation decisions aligned with policy intent, but key implementation gaps were identified and may have been associated with biases in allocation. Explicit documentation, contemporaneous monitoring, and enforcement mechanisms may improve policy implementation during oncology drug shortages.

papers.abstract_en: IMPORTANCE: Guideline-discordant care for acute low back pain (aLBP) is common and has been associated with adverse outcomes. OBJECTIVES: To estimate the incidence of new opioid use disorder (OUD) or overdose diagnosis among opioid-naive patients with Medicaid coverage initiating treatment for aLBP and to evaluate the association between initial treatment modalities and subsequent risk of OUD or overdose diagnosis. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This retrospective cohort study used data from January 1, 2016, to December 31, 2019, with 13 months of follow-up (1-month exposure assessment followed by 12 months of outcome follow-up) from the Transformed Medicaid Statistical Information System Analytic Files from 25 states that expanded Medicaid under the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act by 2014. Participants included opioid-naive, adults aged less than 65 years who received pain treatment within 1 month of diagnosis of aLBP. Data were analyzed from March 1, 2025, to July 31, 2026. EXPOSURES: Initial pharmacologic and nonpharmacologic treatments for aLBP. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: OUD or overdose diagnosis, defined using diagnostic codes for opioid abuse, opioid dependence, opioid-involved overdose, or a prescription for medication for treating OUD. RESULTS: In this cohort of  399 500 Medicaid patients who initiated treatment for newly diagnosed aLBP, the median age was 39 (IQR, 30-50) years, and 237 846 (59.5%) were female. The cumulative incidence of OUD or overdose diagnosis was 1.4% at 7 months and 2.3% at 13 months. Initiating vs not initiating higher-dose opioids (>50 mg of morphine equivalent) as part of the initial treatment was associated with the greatest risk, increasing risk of OUD or overdose by 146.6% (95% CI, 121.5%-171.7%). Initiating vs not initiating lower-dose opioids prescribed for more than 7 days or gabapentinoids each increased risk by 105.2% (95% CI, 89.0%-121.4%) and 101.6% (95% CI, 84.9%-118.2%), respectively. Nonpharmacologic, noninterventional therapies were associated with reductions in risk of OUD or overdose diagnosis. Initiating vs not initiating chiropractic care was associated with the largest relative risk reduction, decreasing risk by 32.8% (95% CI, 26.8%-38.9%), and initiating physical therapy was associated with 31.1% decreased risk (95% CI, 22.1%-40.1%). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cohort study, nonpharmacologic, noninterventional treatment was associated with reductions in risk of OUD or overdose diagnosis while initiating treatment with opioids or gabapentinoids was each associated with higher risks. These results support guideline recommendations favoring nonpharmacologic treatments as first-line therapy for aLBP.

papers.abstract_en: IMPORTANCE: Clinical data comparing time to presentation and stroke quality metrics for intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) and acute ischemic stroke (AIS) are limited. Understanding these differences is essential to provide timely care to all stroke subtypes. OBJECTIVE: To compare prehospital and emergency department (ED) process quality metrics between patients with ICH and AIS. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Cohort study included patients with AIS and ICH admitted to Get With The Guidelines (GWTG)-Stroke participating hospitals from January 1, 2015, to June 30, 2024, who arrived by emergency medical services (EMS). Data were analyzed from 195 hospitals across the US. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Prehospital-based and ED-based process metrics (eg, EMS prenotification, door to ED physician assessment time, door to initial brain imaging order) were assessed. Logistic and linear regression models were sequentially adjusted for patient demographics, medical history and presenting factors, and hospital characteristics. Temporal trends of prehospital care metrics were examined. RESULTS: A total of 195 659 patients (median [IQR] age, 74.0 [63.0-83.0] years; 97 978 [50.1%] female; 31 464 with ICH and 164 195 with AIS) from 195 hospitals were included. The median (IQR) National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score was 14 (6-23) for ICH vs 6 (2-13) for AIS (absolute standardized difference, 0.694). ICH (vs AIS) was associated with higher odds of door-to-ED physician assessment of 10 or fewer minutes after adjusting for patient demographics (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.08; 95% CI, 1.02-1.14). This association reversed after adding adjustment for medical history and presenting factors (including NIHSS) and hospital characteristics (aOR, 0.94; 95% CI, 0.89-0.99). This pattern was observed for door to initial brain imaging order of 20 or fewer minutes (demographic-adjusted: aOR, 1.09; 95% CI, 1.02-1.16; fully adjusted with medical history and hospital characteristics: aOR, 0.91; 95% CI, 0.85-0.97). Median last known well to arrival time increased by 32.5% for AIS (151 to 200 minutes; P < .001) and 34.3% for ICH (108 to 145 minutes; P < .001), while rates of EMS prenotification largely remained stable for both ICH and AIS. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cohort study of patients with acute stroke, patients with ICH arrived at the ED faster but were less likely to achieve care targets. In the context of emerging hyperacute ICH therapies and bundled care models, addressing these differences is essential to optimizing acute stroke outcomes.

papers.abstract_en: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related deaths worldwide. Leptomeningeal metastasis (LM), a serious complication of advanced lung cancer, poses significant challenges in both clinical diagnosis and treatment monitoring, and is associated with a poor prognosis. Conventional diagnostic methods include magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) cytology; however, their sensitivity is limited, particularly in the early stages of the disease. Against this backdrop, liquid biopsy has emerged as a minimally invasive and practical approach for molecular assessment and longitudinal monitoring of LM. Recent studies have reported that, in selected cohorts of patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and LM, CSF-derived circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) detects driver and resistance-associated alterations more frequently than paired plasma, while epithelial cell adhesion molecule (EpCAM)-based CSF circulating tumor cell (CTC) assays have reported sensitivities of 76%-100% and specificities of 84%-100%, compared with a first-lumbar-puncture sensitivity of 44%-67% for conventional CSF cytology. These performance estimates should be interpreted in the context of selected cohorts and heterogeneous reference frameworks. Furthermore, cerebrospinal fluid circulating tumor cell (CSF-CTC) burden holds prognostic value, with higher CTC levels associated with poorer survival outcomes. This review summarizes recent advances in liquid biopsy biomarkers including ctDNA, DNA methylation, microRNA (miRNA), proteins, and circulating tumor cells (CTCs), focusing on their applications in the diagnosis, treatment monitoring, and prognostic assessment of lung cancer-associated LM, and provides a comparative discussion of liquid biopsy based on plasma and cerebrospinal fluid specimens. It further explores the potential, current challenges, and directions for clinical translation of multi-omics integration in the personalized management of LM.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) is a complex procedure, and there is a significant shortage of trained practitioners in China. AIM: To evaluate effectiveness of a structured ERCP training program at a national training center and identify key determinants of success. METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted among 68 graduates (response rate 62.5%) of the ERCP training program at Beijing Friendship Hospital (2017-2024). Data on demographics, training content, and post-training ERCP practice were collected via questionnaire. Primary competence was defined as performing > 10 ERCPs annually with a cannulation success rate ≥ 70% (entry-level). A secondary analysis used the > 90% cannulation rate (advanced mastery) to align with international benchmarks. Multivariate logistic regression identified factors associated with competence. RESULTS: Most trainees (83.8%) successfully performed ERCP post-training; 63.2% achieved entry-level competence, while only 25.0% reached the advanced ≥ 90% standard. Subgroup analysis showed that 3-month and 6-month groups achieved higher entry-level competence (69.6% and 67.7%, respectively) than the 12-month group (42.9%), attributed to greater weekly hands-on density. Multivariate analysis identified longer training duration (OR 1.32, P = 0.011), greater weekly hands-on opportunities (OR 2.05, P = 0.013), and sufficient mentor guidance (OR 3.49, P = 0.016) as independent predictors. CONCLUSION: The structured ERCP training program effectively establishes entry-level competence for most trainees, but achieving international mastery remains challenging. Success is associated with adequate training duration, frequent hands-on experience, and quality mentorship. We propose a tiered accreditation system and post-training remediation pathways to safely address the national shortage of ERCPists.

Insofar as the extent of tumour response correlates with metrics of patient survival, this underscores the critical ongoing need for rigorous and reproducible approaches to pathological response assessment following surgery. In the current review, we provide a historical overview of early trials assessing safety and efficacy of neoadjuvant targeted and immune therapy, and we summarize the earliest and revised recommendations for pathological response assessment of treated melanoma specimens. Moreover, we highlight that not only the extent of response but also the composition of that response correlates with recurrence-free survival in these high-risk patients.

papers.abstract_en: Liver-organotropic metastasis occurs in cancers such as uveal melanoma (UM) and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) and is a leading cause of mortality at the terminal stage. Colonization is a rate-limiting and converging step in the metastatic cascade. The drivers underlying liver colonization have largely remained elusive. In this report, we hypothesized that pioneer transcription factors (TFs) increase chromatin accessibility and superenhancer (SE) remodeling, which subsequently promote colonization-associated cellular features [e.g., proliferation, survival, cancer stem cells (CSCs), motility] by driving the transcription of the respective SE-associated genes. We tested this hypothesis and discovered that the pioneer TF KLF4 promoted chromatin accessibility and SE remodeling by ATAC-seq and ChIP-seq. Chromatin accessibility and SE remodeling significantly increased the transcription of the SE-associated genes MCL1 and RASGRP3, which consequently promoted proliferation, motility, and metastasis. Furthermore, the upregulation of KLF4 expression in UM cells was promoted by RN7SL2-containing exosomes from surrounding endothelial cells. Analysis of clinical datasets revealed that the overexpression of RIG-I, STAT1, KLF4, and RASGRP3 was individually correlated with shorter metastasis-free survival or overall survival in patients with UM and PDAC. In conclusion, the identification of the exoRN7SL2-STAT1-KLF4-SEs-RASGRP3 signaling axis may help elucidate metastatic colonization through interactions between tumor cells and the endothelial niche and may yield novel and viable therapeutic targets.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The optimal surgical approach for patients with low-risk differentiated thyroid cancer (DTC) remains controversial. Current evidence comparing long-term outcomes between total thyroidectomy and hemithyroidectomy is limited by short follow-up and a lack of comprehensive patient-reported outcomes. OBJECTIVE: To compare the effectiveness of total thyroidectomy versus hemithyroidectomy in patients with low-risk DTC, evaluating oncologic outcomes, complications, thyroid function, quality of life, and healthcare costs. METHODS: We conducted a multicenter retrospective cohort study of 800 patients with low-risk DTC treated at three tertiary centers between 2014 and 2021, with follow-up through 2023. Propensity score matching (1:1) was performed using age, sex, tumor size, histology, and BRAF V600E status. Patients were analyzed according to the operation actually performed (as-treated analysis). Primary outcomes were overall survival and recurrence-free survival. Secondary outcomes included complications, thyroid function, quality of life (HADS, SCL-90), and healthcare costs. Analyses included Kaplan-Meier survival analysis with log-rank tests and Cox proportional-hazards regression, with Bonferroni correction for the two primary endpoints. RESULTS: After propensity score matching, 400 patients were included in each group (median follow-up 7.2 years, IQR 5.1-8.9). The 8-year overall survival rates were 97.2% (95% CI 95.6-98.8%) for total thyroidectomy versus 96.1% (95% CI 94.2-97.9%) for hemithyroidectomy (HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.44-1.42, p = 0.43). The 8-year recurrence-free survival rates were 96.8% versus 94.2% (HR 1.48, 95% CI 0.73-2.98, p = 0.28). Hemithyroidectomy was associated with a significantly lower rate of permanent hypoparathyroidism (2.0% vs 8.0%, p < 0.001, NNH = 17). Total thyroidectomy entailed a universal requirement for lifelong levothyroxine (100% vs 15% requiring replacement in the hemithyroidectomy group); among hemithyroidectomy patients not requiring replacement, subclinical hypothyroidism was common. At one year, fewer hemithyroidectomy patients reported clinically significant anxiety/depression (18% vs 25%, p = 0.018). Mean total 8-year healthcare costs were lower with hemithyroidectomy (¥28,247 vs ¥55,439, p < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: For appropriately selected patients with low-risk DTC, hemithyroidectomy provides oncologic outcomes comparable to total thyroidectomy while offering advantages in complications, thyroid-function preservation, quality of life, and healthcare costs. Treatment decisions should be individualized through shared decision-making. These findings support consideration of de-escalated surgery but require validation in prospective randomized trials.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Surgical stabilization of rib fractures (SSRF) is increasingly used in the management of traumatic rib fractures, but its in-hospital outcomes in high-altitude trauma settings remain uncertain. We evaluated the association of SSRF with in-hospital pulmonary complications and length of stay in a high-altitude (≈ 3,500 m) trauma system. METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study of adults with CT-confirmed traumatic rib fractures admitted from 2015 to 2023 and managed with SSRF or non-operative management. Confounding was addressed using stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) with augmented outcome models; overlap weighting, propensity score matching, and time-dependent exposure analysis were used as sensitivity analyses. The primary outcome was a composite of in-hospital pneumonia, atelectasis, or respiratory failure. Pulmonary risk ratios (RRs) were estimated using modified Poisson regression, while ICU and hospital length of stay were analyzed using log-transformed weighted models. RESULTS: Among 324 patients, 121 underwent SSRF and 203 received non-operative management. Before adjustment, SSRF patients had greater injury severity. In IPTW-augmented analyses, the pulmonary estimate was imprecise (RR 0.86, 95% CI 0.23-3.21; P = 0.822), and no significant difference was detected in ICU length of stay (exp[β] 1.04, 95% CI 0.97-1.10; P = 0.286). Hospital length of stay was longer with SSRF (exp[β] 2.31, 95% CI 2.02-2.65; P < 0.001). CONCLUSION: Adjusted analyses found no statistically detectable difference in pulmonary complications or ICU length of stay, although the pulmonary estimate remained imprecise and does not establish equivalence or safety. SSRF was associated with longer hospital length of stay. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Not applicable.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Immune-mediated non-infectious uveitis (NIU) is a leading cause of blindness in high-income countries. Adalimumab is the only licensed non-corticosteroid drug for non-infectious intermediate, posterior or panuveitis. We evaluated the efficacy, safety and cost-effectiveness of an adalimumab biosimilar as add-on therapy for a broad NIU population. METHODS: This multicentre, placebo-controlled randomised trial recruited adults with sight-threatening or controlled NIU requiring oral prednisolone >5 mg/day from 18 UK NHS ophthalmology departments between 29 July 2021 and 7 June 2024. After a 16-week treatment run-in (TRI) with adalimumab, responders (prednisolone ≤5 mg/day, no active disease) were randomised 1:1 (parallel groups; concealed web-based allocation) to fortnightly subcutaneous 40 mg adalimumab (biosimilar) or placebo as add-on therapy; all but the trial statistician were masked. The primary outcome, time to treatment failure (TF; disease activity or prednisolone >5 mg/day), was analysed at 12 months by intention to treat. The health economic evaluation was pre-specified in the trial protocol; we estimated incremental cost per TF avoided, NHS perspective. Registered: ISRCTN31474800. FINDINGS: 182 participants completed the TRI, 119 (65.4%) responded, and 115 were randomised (60 adalimumab, 55 placebo). At 12 months, 31.4% (adalimumab) and 59.0% (placebo) had experienced TF (hazard ratio 0.42, 95% CI 0.23-0.75, p = 0.003). Among patients ineligible for NHS treatment (85%), the effect was similar (hazard ratio 0.37, 95% CI 0.20-0.71, p = 0.003). Adverse events were similarly frequent; two were serious, one per group. Incremental cost was £2320 per TF avoided. INTERPRETATION: Adalimumab added to standard care reduces treatment failure in NIU, including in patients with macular oedema, unilateral disease, and steroid-dependent inactive uveitis, and is affordable. Future work should identify complementary treatments for disease refractory to adalimumab. FUNDING: Health Technology Assessment Programme, National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR); Biogen International GmbH (Baar, Switzerland) provided the placebo for the trial.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: To identify clinical and routine sacroiliac joint (SIJ) MRI variables associated with structural damage progression in axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA). MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective longitudinal study enrolled 234 patients with axSpA who underwent at least two SIJ MRI examinations between August 2011 and March 2024 (643 examinations, 409 consecutive visit pairs). Progression at each follow-up examination relative to the previous one was adjudicated using an SSS-based three-step algorithm. Mixed-effects logistic regression with patient-specific random intercepts identified factors associated with progression, with the MRI follow-up interval as a covariate. Multicollinearity was assessed using variance inflation factors, and treatment exposure was evaluated in a sensitivity analysis. RESULTS: Progression was identified in 260 of 409 follow-up examinations (63.6%). After adjustment for the MRI follow-up interval, a higher erosion SSS score (odds ratio [OR] 1.178, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.099-1.262, P < 0.001), smoking (OR 2.023, 95% CI 1.091-3.751, P = 0.025), and HLA-B27 positivity (OR 2.929, 95% CI 1.225-7.007, P = 0.016) were independently associated with increased progression risk, whereas older age at diagnosis (OR 0.970, 95% CI 0.946-0.993, P = 0.012) was associated with decreased risk; these associations were essentially unchanged after forced entry of treatment exposure. CONCLUSION: A higher erosion burden at the previous examination, smoking, and HLA-B27 positivity were associated with SIJ structural damage progression; patients diagnosed at a younger age also warrant attention. Given the retrospective observational design, these are statistical associations whose causality and clinical utility require prospective validation.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) is a leading cause of anovulatory infertility. Although follicular developmental arrest is a defining feature of PMOS, the cell-type-specific mechanisms linking genetic susceptibility, endocrine imbalance and follicular microenvironmental dysfunction remain incompletely understood, particularly across clinical subtypes. METHODS: We performed single-cell RNA sequencing of preovulatory follicular-fluid cells from healthy controls and women with uncomplicated PMOS, hyperandrogenic PMOS and metformin-treated insulin-resistant PMOS. We integrated these data with GWAS-derived disease relevance scores and ovarian chromatin-accessibility annotations to map genetic risk to follicular cell populations and regulatory programmes. Ligand-receptor analyses were used to infer intercellular communication networks. Transcriptomic metabolic findings were further assessed by follicular-fluid metabolic and steroid-hormone measurements, DHT-treated granulosa-cell functional assays, and reanalysis of a DHEA-induced mouse PMOS-like ovarian dataset. RESULTS: We generated a single-cell atlas of the PMOS follicular microenvironment comprising 220,983 high-quality cells. Granulosa cells showed the strongest enrichment of PMOS-related genetic risk, with regulatory-genetic support from ovarian snATAC-seq integration. Among granulosa cell states, a GC2_CYP19A1⁺ population was preferentially associated with hyperandrogenic PMOS and displayed a transcriptional programme characterized by steroidogenic remodelling coupled to reduced energy-metabolic activity. Biochemical profiling supported this endocrine-metabolic imbalance, showing increased follicular-fluid androstenedione (ASD) and estrone, reduced estradiol and E2/ASD ratio, decreased ATP, citrate and fumarate hydratase activity, and increased lactate and β-hydroxybutyrate. Prolonged DHT exposure impaired granulosa-cell mitochondrial respiration, ATP production and mitochondrial membrane potential. In parallel, PMOS subtypes showed immune remodelling and altered ligand-receptor signalling, with hyperandrogenic PMOS associated with increased inflammatory signalling and reduced homeostatic or tissue-repair pathways. Reanalysis of a DHEA-induced mouse ovarian dataset provided supportive evidence for androgen-associated steroidogenic pathway perturbation. CONCLUSIONS: This study provides a cell-resolved framework linking PMOS genetic susceptibility to endocrine-metabolic and immune remodelling in the preovulatory follicular microenvironment. The identification of a hyperandrogen-associated GC2_CYP19A1⁺ state highlights a candidate cellular programme in which steroidogenic imbalance is coupled to impaired granulosa-cell bioenergetics. These findings provide a resource for future validation and may inform microenvironment-guided stratification of PMOS and the development of strategies aimed at restoring follicular function.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Obesity is a multifactorial disorder with a substantial yet incompletely defined genetic component. Rare monogenic variants, particularly in consanguineous populations, may account for part of the 'missing heritability.' OBJECTIVES: To delineate the genetic contribution to severe obesity in individuals from Saudi Arabia by pinpointing known and novel monogenic variants in families presenting with extreme phenotypes. METHODS: Eight multiplex Saudi families (each comprising 9 members; range: lean body weight to severe obesity) were enrolled. Adults had a BMI of ≥30 kg/m2; children exceeded the 90th percentile (overweight) or the 97th percentile (obese). Whole-exome sequencing (WES) was performed on samples collected from two children in each family, including one child with obesity and one control child without obesity. Variant calling files were filtered for quality, frequency < 1%, and predicted functional impact. Candidate loci were prioritized using Moon (Diploid) software and manual curation, then validated by Sanger sequencing. RESULTS: Initial filtering revealed 40 rare, potentially pathogenic variants in 35 genes shared among affected relatives. Prioritization highlighted 28 variants in 19 candidate genes, encompassing established obesity-related genes (e.g. LEPR, MC4R, BDNF) and putative novel loci linked to appetite regulation, lipid metabolism, and energy balance. Segregation analysis identified both heterozygous and homozygous variants across affected individuals, reflecting variability in inheritance patterns. Seven previously reported candidate genes did not show pathogenic variants in this cohort. Carriers of prioritized variants exhibited significantly higher BMI z-scores than non-carriers (P < 0.01), underscoring a clear genotype-phenotype correlation. CONCLUSION: This study broadens the catalog of genes associated with obesity in the Saudi population and demonstrates the value of studying extreme phenotypes in consanguineous families. Both previously recognized and novel variants were identified in association with severe, early-onset obesity, reflecting genetic heterogeneity across families rather than a single underlying mechanism. These findings provide a foundation for improved genetic characterization, tailored counseling, and future functional studies.

papers.abstract_en: Source-Free Unsupervised Domain Adaptation (SFUDA) has emerged as a critical paradigm for addressing severe domain shifts in medical image segmentation under strict data privacy constraints, where source data are inaccessible. However, existing SFUDA methods primarily rely on static, open-loop adaptation pipelines, lacking the ability to actively perceive target domain characteristics and use reflection to correct accumulated errors. Meanwhile, Vision Foundation Models (VFMs) and Vision Language Models (VLMs) exhibit strong generalization across modalities and anatomies, yet their high computational inference overhead and deployment constraints prevent direct adoption on clinical edge devices. In this work, we propose PARDA, a VLM-coupled closed-loop SFUDA framework for medical image segmentation. PARDA reformulates SFUDA as a closed-loop decision-making process, in which the method actively perceives target domain characteristics, acts by coordinating semantic and geometric VFMs to generate pseudo-labels, reflects on the reliability of its anatomical and structural representations to guide refinement, and finally distills the acquired adaptation knowledge into a lightweight student model. This design enables PARDA to mitigate error accumulation while preserving data privacy and inference efficiency. We conduct a comprehensive SFUDA evaluation covering 13 cross-modality domain adaptation directions and 24 anatomical targets across diverse organs and imaging modalities. Experimental results demonstrate that PARDA achieves robust and universal domain adaptation while distilling the adaptation results into a lightweight student model for resource-constrained inference.

papers.abstract_en: IMPORTANCE: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is associated with adverse life outcomes and increased mortality. Clarifying the magnitude of mortality risks using international data and the potential association between medication and mortality is essential to inform clinical care and motivate public health strategies to address mortality. OBJECTIVES: To examine the association between ADHD and all-cause and cause-specific mortality and to assess whether mortality risk differs according to ADHD medication use. DATA SOURCES: A comprehensive search of PubMed, Web of Science, PsycINFO, EMBASE, MEDLINE, and CINAHL was conducted from database inception to July 8, 2025. STUDY SELECTION: Eligible studies included quantitative research across all age groups reporting all-cause and/or cause-specific mortality in individuals with ADHD, defined via diagnostic criteria, self-identification, trait measures, or ADHD polygenic risk scores. Exclusion criteria were nonoriginal research, qualitative studies, non-peer-reviewed publications, and studies not reporting mortality outcomes. DATA EXTRACTION AND SYNTHESIS: Data extraction was conducted independently by 2 reviewers. Study quality was assessed by 1 reviewer. Summary data were extracted from published reports, and pooled hazard ratios (HRs) were calculated using random-effects model meta-analysis. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcomes were all-cause mortality and cause-specific mortality (suicide, unintentional or intentional injury, and natural causes), measured using HRs with 95% CIs. RESULTS: Nineteen studies including 15 920 970 participants (36.1% female) were included. ADHD was associated with increased all-cause mortality (HR, 1.71; 95% CI, 1.31-2.24; P < .001). Significant associations were also observed for suicide (HR, 1.89; 95% CI, 1.21-2.95; P = .005), unintentional or intentional injury (HR, 1.55; 95% CI, 1.22-2.00; P < .001), and natural-cause mortality (HR, 1.27; 95% CI, 1.16-1.38; P < .001). ADHD medication use in people with ADHD was associated with reduced all-cause mortality (HR, 0.75; 95% CI, 0.64-0.87; P < .001). Substantial heterogeneity was observed across studies. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this systematic review and meta-analysis of ADHD and mortality, ADHD was associated with increased mortality across multiple causes; and ADHD medication was associated with a decreased all-cause mortality risk, underscoring the importance of timely diagnosis and treatment. However, the heterogeneity observed across studies highlights the need for standardized methods and improved control of confounding factors to better characterize mortality risk among individuals with ADHD.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Transanal total mesorectal excision (taTME) was introduced to improve distal dissection in low rectal cancer, but some previous studies have concerns about increased local recurrence during taTME. RESULTS: A total of 306 patients were included, of whom 94 underwent taTME and 212 underwent R-TME between 2008 and 2018. There were no significant differences in OS, DFS, LRFS, or DRFS between two groups. After 1:1 propensity score matching, 88 matched pairs were generated, and matched analyses also showed no statistically significant association between surgical approach and OS, DFS, LRFS, or DRFS. In subgroup analyses stratified by yp stage, yT stage, and by unfavorable factors (male, BMI ≥ 25 kg/m2, and undergoing nCRT), long-term oncologic outcomes showed similar between taTME and R-TME. papers.abstract_en: Low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) reduces radiation exposure but introduces spatially heterogeneous noise and artifacts that can obscure subtle anatomical structures. We address post-reconstruction image-domain LDCT restoration, where degradation suppression and structure preservation impose competing demands on a single restoration trajectory. We propose DSAUNet, a Dual-State Adaptive Unrolled Network that maintains persistent anatomy- and degradation-oriented latent states across unrolled stages. Rather than acting as transient feature branches, the evolving states participate in parameterizing subsequent restoration behavior through a degradation-oriented global policy coordinate for stage-level modulation and state-derived confidence variables for spatially selective regulation. Direction-aware prior modeling and multi-scale state guidance further realize this state-parameterized restoration process. Under the reported protocols, DSAUNet achieves 40.3721 dB PSNR and 0.9642 SSIM on 2DeteCT, exceeding the strongest baseline by 1.6320 dB and 0.0108, and achieves 47.4277 dB PSNR and 0.9846 SSIM under the patient-level five-fold Mayo evaluation, with a 1.0920 dB PSNR gain over the strongest PSNR baseline. On LoDoPaB-CT, it further obtains 38.5501 dB PSNR and 0.9141 SSIM, with the best PSNR, SSIM, and VIF among the compared methods. Controlled raw-state, persistent state-swapping, policy-coordinate, and confidence-map analyses support functionally differentiated state roles and active adaptive regulation. Bidirectional 2DeteCT-Mayo zero-shot experiments reveal direction-dependent transfer behavior, while unified profiling characterizes an accuracy-complexity trade-off. Together, these results support persistent dual-state controlled unrolling as a structured approach to image-domain LDCT restoration within the evaluated settings.

papers.abstract_en: MYT1L-Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder (MYT1L-NDD) is a rare autosomal dominant syndrome characterized by intellectual disability, global developmental delay, autism, and obesity. Despite growing recognition, prospective and systematic clinical phenotyping remains limited. Here, we present an exploratory analysis of data from 25 individuals with MYT1L-NDD enrolled in the Brain Gene Registry (BGR), a national platform integrating genetic, neurobehavioral, and clinical data. Neurobehavioral assessments were conducted using the Rapid Neurobehavioral Assessment Protocol (RNAP), including virtual adaptations of the Shipley, Developmental Profile-4, ASEBA Child Behavior Checklist, and Vineland-3. Diagnostic and medication data were extracted from structured electronic health records (EHR). MYT1L-NDD participants were compared to the broader BGR cohort. MYT1L-NDD participants exhibited pronounced impairments in nonverbal cognition and adaptive functioning, particularly in motor tasks, communication, and daily living skills. Behavioral assessments revealed elevated rates of autism symptoms, ADHD symptoms, behavioral conduct problems, oppositional defiance, and anxiety. EHR diagnosis data were available for 10 MYT1L-NDD participants. It showed frequent diagnoses of developmental delays, speech and language disorders, intellectual disability, gastrointestinal problems, and obesity. Medication data on five participants indicated common prescription of alpha-2 adrenergic agonists and laxatives. This study provides the first prospective, multi-source characterization of MYT1L-NDD. Findings expand our understanding of MYT1L-NDD phenotypes in a quantitative and systematic manner and support the value of registry-based approaches for understanding rare neurodevelopmental disorders. Larger, longitudinal, age-stratified studies are needed to further define MYT1L-NDD natural history and inform clinical care.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Distinguishing complicated from uncomplicated appendicitis before surgery remains a critical yet unresolved clinical challenge. Delayed recognition of complicated appendicitis, particularly in cases of perforation or abscess formation, is associated with increased morbidity and mortality. Although various laboratory markers and inflammatory indices have been proposed as markers associated with disease severity, their relative diagnostic performance remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate and compare the discriminatory performance of conventional laboratory parameters, leukocyte-derived indices, and composite biomarkers for complicated appendicitis. METHODS: In this retrospective single-center cohort study, 5,428 patients who underwent emergency appendectomy between 2015 and 2025 were included. Patients were classified as uncomplicated or complicated appendicitis based on intraoperative findings. Preoperative laboratory parameters, including C-reactive protein, white blood cell count, total bilirubin, leukocyte-derived indices, and composite biomarkers such as the C-reactive protein-albumin-lymphocyte (CALLY) index and the hemoglobin-albumin-lymphocyte-platelet (HALP) index, were analyzed. Receiver operating characteristic analysis was used to assess diagnostic performance, and optimal cut-off values were determined using the Youden index. Multivariate logistic regression was performed to identify variables independently associated with complicated appendicitis. RESULTS: Of the 5,428 patients, 707 (13.1%) had complicated appendicitis. C-reactive protein demonstrated the highest diagnostic accuracy (AUC: 0.781) and demonstrated the strongest independent association (OR: 5.29). Total bilirubin was also independently associated with complicated appendicitis (OR: 1.21). Leukocyte-derived indices showed limited discriminatory ability, with only the systemic immune-inflammation index remaining significant in multivariate analysis. The CALLY index demonstrated relatively strong discriminatory performance (AUC: 0.747), with lower values associated with increased disease severity. CONCLUSIONS: C-reactive protein remains the most robust laboratory marker for identifying complicated appendicitis. Composite biomarkers such as the CALLY index may provide additional value in risk stratification. These findings support the use of routinely available laboratory parameters in clinical risk assessment, although prospective validation is warranted.

papers.abstract_en: AIM: The Tubeless comprehensive management model minimizes iatrogenic trauma by avoiding endotracheal intubation, chest tube placement, and urinary catheterization, while the robot-assisted thoracoscopic surgery system offers precise surgical manipulation and high-definition visualization. However, clinical evidence supporting the combination of these two approaches in early-stage lung cancer surgery remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate the short-term safety and clinical benefits of robot-assisted lobectomy based on the Tubeless concept in patients with early-stage lung cancer. METHODS: A total of 120 patients with early-stage non-small cell lung cancer who underwent robot-assisted lobectomy in our department between January 2022 and May 2025 were retrospectively analyzed. According to the perioperative management approach, patients were divided into the Tubeless group (n = 50), which received spontaneous breathing anesthesia without indwelling chest tubes or urinary catheters, and the traditional group (n = 70), which received double-lumen endotracheal intubation with indwelling chest tubes and urinary catheters. Baseline characteristics, intraoperative parameters, postoperative pain scores, postoperative complications, length of hospital stay, patient satisfaction, and 30-day readmission rates were compared between the two groups. RESULTS: No significant differences in baseline characteristics were observed between the two groups (p > 0.05). Similarly, no significant differences were observed in intraoperative blood loss, operative time, number of lymph node dissection stations, or total number of lymph nodes dissected (p > 0.05). Visual analogue scale (VAS) scores on postoperative days 1, 2, and 3 were significantly lower in the Tubeless group than in the traditional group (p < 0.05). The overall incidence of postoperative complications was significantly lower in the Tubeless group than in the traditional group (p = 0.04). Total hospital stay and postoperative hospital stay were significantly shorter in the Tubeless group than in the traditional group (p < 0.001). No significant difference was observed in the 30-day readmission rate between the two groups. CONCLUSIONS: Robot-assisted lobectomy combined with the Tubeless comprehensive management approach is feasible and is associated with favorable short-term perioperative outcomes in patients with early-stage lung cancer. However, long-term oncologic outcomes, such as recurrence-free and overall survival, require further investigation.

papers.abstract_en: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, accounting for approximately 1.8 million deaths annually. Despite advances in targeted therapies and immunotherapy, late diagnosis and therapeutic resistance continue to limit patient outcomes. Emerging evidence implicates systemic inflammation and oxidative stress as critical drivers of lung cancer initiation, progression, and treatment resistance. This comprehensive review synthesizes current knowledge regarding alterations in serum C-reactive protein (CRP), nitric oxide (NO), superoxide dismutase (SOD), glutathione reductase (GR), and glutathione peroxidase (GPx) in patients with lung cancer. A consistent body of literature demonstrates significantly elevated CRP and NO levels alongside markedly reduced SOD, GR, and GPx activities in treatment-naïve patients with lung cancer compared to healthy controls, indicating a profound inflammatory-oxidative imbalance. However, important heterogeneity exists across studies, with the magnitude of these alterations varying by tumor stage, histological subtype, smoking history, and the biological compartment analyzed. The absence of linear correlation between inflammatory and antioxidant markers in several studies suggests complex, non-linear interactions between these pathways rather than simple opposition. Clinically, this combined biomarker panel may aid in risk stratification, disease monitoring, and evaluation of therapeutic response, particularly when integrated into established scoring systems such as the Glasgow Prognostic Score. Major knowledge gaps persist, including a lack of large prospective longitudinal studies, the absence of validated cut-off values, and limited correlation with hard clinical endpoints. Future research should prioritize multicenter cohorts with standardized assays and paired serum-tissue analyses to translate this axis into routine oncologic practice.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Fiducial markers are essential for accurate image-guided stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). However, post-implantation positional variation introduces geometric uncertainty. This study aims to quantify the spatiotemporal observed displacement of fiducial markers in HCC patients treated with CyberKnife SBRT and to identify predictive factors for significant displacement. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed data from 185 HCC patients who underwent percutaneous implantation of 518 fiducial markers between January 2018 and December 2022. Serial CT scans were acquired at baseline (Day 1) and on days 3, 5, 7, 10, and 14 post-implantation. Fiducial displacement was measured in three dimensions (craniocaudal, anteroposterior, mediolateral) relative to the baseline scan after rigid registration to vertebral bodies. Significant displacement was defined as a 3D vector displacement > 3 mm, encompassing true migration and geometrical uncertainties. To account for data clustering (multiple markers per patient), univariate and multivariable Generalized Estimating Equations (GEE) models were used to identify predictors of significant displacement. Internal validation was performed using bootstrap resampling. Furthermore, a dosimetric analysis was conducted to evaluate the clinical impact of significant marker displacement. RESULTS: The mean 3D vector displacement was greatest at Day 3 (2.8 ± 1.5 mm) and progressively decreased, plateauing after Day 7 (Day 7: 1.9 ± 1.1 mm; Day 14: 1.8 ± 1.0 mm; p < 0.001 for trend). The craniocaudal axis exhibited the largest magnitude of displacement. By Day 7, 88.6% of markers achieved stability (displacement ≤ 3 mm). Dosimetric evaluation revealed that simulated displacement > 3 mm significantly degraded target coverage (PTV V100%: 98.5% vs. 92.1%, p < 0.001). Multivariate GEE analysis identified tumor location within 2 cm of the diaphragm (Odds Ratio [OR] = 3.05, 95% CI: 1.75-5.20, p < 0.001) and tumor diameter > 5 cm (OR = 1.98, 95% CI: 1.15-3.30, p = 0.012) as independent predictors for significant fiducialisplacement. The optimism-corrected area under the curve (AUC) for the predictive model was 0.76. CONCLUSION: Fiducial markers in HCC patients undergo significant early displacement, primarily within the first week, and stabilize thereafter. Proximity to the diaphragm and larger tumor size are associated with a higher risk of displacement, which can negatively impact delivered dosimetry in simulated scenarios. These findings support a recommended 7-day waiting period between implantation and CT simulation as a reasonable safety guideline and suggest that patients with high-risk features may benefit from extended monitoring or adaptive radiotherapy strategies.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: To investigate whether the use of a silver beam filtration with deep learning reconstruction (DLR) impact the normal adrenal gland on unenhanced MDCT in terms of density, image quality and radiation dose. METHODS: This unicentric retrospective study evaluated two unenhanced MDCT acquisitions of 123 patients performed with a conventional filtration (Group A) and with a silver filtration (Group B) on a 320-detector row CT scanner with DLR. A total of 246 series, corresponding to 492 adrenal glands, were analyzed. We recorded the HU values of the normal adrenal gland, subcutaneous fat and extra corporeal air as well as the radiation dose and assessed image quality. RESULTS: The subjective image quality was excellent, with no significant difference between the two acquisitions with a mean score on the Likert scale of 4.6 ± 0.3 and 4.1 ± 0.6 for groups A and B, respectively (p = 0.09). Interobserver agreement for image quality was good and quite similar for both groups (group B: k= 0.86; group A: k= 0.90). The mean density of adrenal gland was 15.65 ± 5.5 HU with conventional filtration (Group A) and 13.05 ± 4.5 HU for silver filtration (Group B). For the right adrenal gland, the median values were 15.8 HU and 12.9 HU for group A and B, respectively (p=0.01). For the left adrenal gland, the median values were 15.5 HU and 13.2 HU for group A and B, respectively (p=0.03). A subgroup of 135 adrenal glands (including both right and left side) with a density value ≤ 15HU using conventional filtration (Subgroup A) showed a statistically significant lower median value with silver filtration (Subgroup B). Inside this ≤ 15 HU subgroup, 59 adrenal glands had a density value equal or lower than 10 HU of which 48 belonged to subgroup B. A reduction in HU values of 18% was observed with the silver filter in the overall cohort (492 adrenal glands), and 26% in the subgroup ≤ 15 HU. Similarly, the mean score for image noise was 7.6 ± 1.5 for conventional filter and 8.3 ± 0.9 for silver filtration, with no statistically significant difference (p = 0.08). Radiation dose was significantly reduced by 35% in examinations performed with silver filtration when compared to conventional filter. CONCLUSION: The spontaneous density of normal adrenal gland is lower than previously reported. Implementing silver filtration with DLR in CT acquisition achieves a significant radiation dose reduction while preserving image quality, along with a decrease in adrenal gland HU values, often below 10 HU. This must be taken into account as this is the threshold of the key reference for adenoma. TRIAL REGISTRATION: This study is part of a routine clinical practice. This unicentric retrospective study was approved by our local institutional review board, and written informed patient consent was not required. The patients were orally informed that their second CT examination will be performed using the newest technology available on the CT machine in our department.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Total knee arthroplasty (TKA) is the standard treatment for end-stage knee osteoarthritis (KOA). Aseptic loosening of the tibial component is a common complication following TKA. Previous studies have indicated that reduced cement volume and thinner cement mantles can lead to stress concentration in the cancellous bone beneath the tibial plateau, which serves as an etiological basis for prosthetic loosening. Our preliminary study has shown that variations in cement distribution can alter the local biomechanical environment. Asymmetric cement distribution is a frequently observed clinical phenomenon; however, no study has yet investigated its impact on the risk of prosthetic loosening. METHODS: A three-dimensional model of the tibial side following total knee arthroplasty was constructed. The model included the tibial cortex, cancellous bone, polyethylene insert, tibial tray, and bone cement. Three model groups were created based on the coronal plane distribution of the cement: symmetric cement distribution, 75% of cement on the tibial side (medial), and 75% of cement on the fibular side (lateral). The model with symmetrical cement distribution achieved cement thickness exceeding 2 mm on both sides. In contrast, in models with asymmetrical cement distribution, the cement thickness on the thinner side fell below this threshold. All models were subjected to a 2100 N compressive load at flexion angles of 0°, 30°, and 60°, under both varus and valgus loading conditions. The differences in compressive stress distribution within the cancellous bone beneath the tibial plateau were analyzed across the models to predict the risk of prosthetic loosening. RESULTS: In models with asymmetric cement distribution, a pronounced stress concentration trend was observed in the cancellous bone on the thinner cement side. Under varus and valgus loading conditions, the load borne by the cancellous bone on the thicker cement side decreased compared to the symmetric distribution model, with the extent of this reduction being smaller than the increase in stress on the thinner cement side. Under axial loading conditions, the peak stress in the asymmetric cement distribution model was consistently higher than that in the symmetric model. A more substantial increase in peak stress was observed when the lateral cement layer was thinner. CONCLUSION: Asymmetric cement distribution leads to an aggravated trend of compressive stress concentration in the cancellous bone on the side with a thinner cement mantle, where the cement thickness is less than 2 mm, the threshold for prosthesis loosening reported by published studies. This serves as a risk factor for increased aseptic loosening of the prosthesis.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The learning curve of laparoscopic distal pancreatectomy (LDP) has traditionally been assessed using global operative indicators such as operative time and blood loss. However, little is known about how technical performance evolves during individual operative steps. This study aimed to perform a workflow-oriented learning curve analysis of LDP using cumulative sum (CUSUM) methodology and step-specific operative assessment. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 58 consecutive patients who underwent LDP between January 2023 and December 2025 at a high-volume pancreatic center. Operative workflow was divided into predefined operative steps according to anatomical landmarks. CUSUM analysis based on operative time was used to identify the transition from the initial phases to the proficiency phase. RESULTS: CUSUM analysis identified a transition point at approximately Case 29. Mean operative time decreased from 77 ± 13 min in the early phase to 54 ± 14 min in the late phase (P < 0.001). The steepest reductions occurred during pancreatic mobilization (31 ± 10 vs. 17 ± 6 min, P < 0.001) and splenic vessel dissection (24 ± 9 vs. 12 ± 4 min, P < 0.001). Estimated blood loss also declined significantly (39 ± 18 vs. 21 ± 11 mL, P = 0.002), while postoperative pancreatic fistula rates and overall complication rates remained comparable between phases. CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort, reductions in operative time during LDP were concentrated in anatomically complex dissection steps rather than uniform acceleration of the entire procedure. Step-specific analysis describes temporal patterns that characterize technical change during minimally invasive pancreatic surgery.

papers.abstract_en: Thauvin-Robinet-Faivre syndrome (TROFAS, OMIM #617107) is a recently identified autosomal recessive disorder characterised by syndromic overgrowth, facial dysmorphism, mild intellectual disability, variable congenital anomalies, and occasional tumour occurrence. TROFAS results from homozygous or compound heterozygous variants in the FIBP gene, encoding the intracellular binding protein for acidic fibroblast growth factor. This protein plays a role in the fibroblast growth factor (FGF) signalling pathway, which is involved in cell proliferation and contributes to the development of several structures, such as the nervous system, optic vesicles, and blood vessels. Prior to the present report, TROFAS has been described in 10 patients from seven families, four of which are of Turkish origin. We report two additional Turkish siblings from a previously unreported family harbouring the recurrent homozygous c.412-3_415dupCAGTTTG likely pathogenic variant in FIBP. Both presented with typical TROFAS features; however, the male sibling exhibited a more severe neurodevelopmental profile and additional malformations, including postaxial polydactyly and upper lip vascular malformation, which, to our knowledge, have not previously been reported in association with TROFAS. A detailed clinical characterisation of these two new cases contributes to a more comprehensive delineation of the syndrome, adding potentially novel phenotypic features requiring confirmation in additional patients.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Radioresistance remains a major barrier to improving radiotherapy (RT) efficacy in colorectal cancer (CRC). Since mitotic fidelity and centrosome homeostasis influence cell fate under genotoxic stress, we investigated whether CFI-400945 enhances the radiation response in CRC models and whether this effect is associated with polo-like kinase 4 (PLK4)-related mitotic dysregulation. METHODS: HCT116 and HT29 CRC cells were treated with CFI-400945 and/or irradiation. Radiation response was evaluated using MTT viability and clonogenic survival assays, alongside analyses of cell-cycle distribution, centrosome-associated abnormalities, nuclear phenotypes, DNA damage-associated signaling, and apoptotic markers. PLK4 involvement was evaluated using siRNA-mediated PLK4 depletion, and Aurora kinase B (AURKB) phosphorylation was assessed to examine potential Aurora B-related effects. Combination treatment was also tested in non-malignant CCD 841 CoN colon-derived control cells and patient-derived CRC organoids. RESULTS: Combined CFI-400945 and RT treatment reduced short-term viability and long-term clonogenic survival in HCT116 and HT29 cells compared with either monotherapy. In CCD 841 CoN cells, CFI-400945 did not significantly enhance radiation-associated loss of clonogenic survival versus RT alone. Combination treatment increased G2/M accumulation, >4 N and sub-G1 fractions, γ-tubulin-positive foci, multinucleation, and micronucleation, consistent with centrosome-associated mitotic abnormalities and reduced survival. DNA damage-associated signaling was enhanced, with increased DNA-dependent protein kinase catalytic subunit (DNA-PKcs) and phosphorylated histone H2AX (γH2AX) levels and increased phosphorylation of ataxia telangiectasia mutated (ATM) and CHK2. Apoptotic marker induction also increased, including robust cleavage of caspase-3 and PARP1. CFI-400945 did not markedly suppress AURKB phosphorylation under the experimental conditions. Importantly, siRNA-mediated PLK4 depletion reduced clonogenic survival after irradiation and increased cleaved PARP1 and cleaved caspase-3, supporting PLK4 involvement in the radiation response. In patient-derived CRC organoids, combination treatment reduced viability and increased DNA damage-associated and apoptotic markers compared with single treatments. CONCLUSIONS: CFI-400945 enhanced radiation response in CRC cell lines and patient-derived organoids, accompanied by centrosome-associated mitotic abnormalities, increased DNA damage-associated signaling, and apoptotic marker induction. siRNA-mediated PLK4 depletion partially recapitulated these effects, supporting a role for PLK4-associated mitotic regulation. However, because CFI-400945 may also target non-PLK4 mitotic kinases, these support an association --between radiosensitization and PLK4-related mitotic dysregulation rather than an exclusively PLK4-dependent mechanism.

papers.abstract_en: Routine primary care encounters offer a major opportunity to reach a large population of individuals eligible for lung cancer screening (LCS) in the U.S., potentially representing up to one-third of all primary care visits each year. This article, the first in a two-part integrative review, synthesizes evidence on the contextual factors that enable or constrain the normalization of guideline-based LCS processes in U.S. primary care. Seven electronic databases were searched in February 2025 (updated in December 2025) to identify relevant studies. The findings reported here draw on 146 studies integrated using thematic synthesis. Four main themes emerged: (1) leadership and policy decisions shaping LCS priorities; (2) alignment of guideline-concordant LCS processes with primary care capacity; (3) frontline adaptations and workarounds sustaining routine LCS delivery; and (4) reframing organizational norms to institutionalize guideline-concordant LCS in primary care. Our review revealed limited health system-level investment in formal screening governance and integrated clinical informatics infrastructure. Normalization required continuous negotiation among providers to reconcile persistent misalignments between guideline demands and primary care capacity. Notably, frontline providers and staff relied heavily on pragmatic adjustments and workarounds, enabling screening to continue through labor-intensive and often fragile processes. Providers operated within and sometimes perpetuated entrenched clinical heuristics and paternalistic traditions while navigating heavy documentation burdens and structural inequities that continued to position LCS as optional, controversial, or administratively burdensome. LCS implementation remains largely provider-driven in contemporary U.S. primary care. Normalization will require deliberate and sustained leadership and policy reform, alongside investments in workforce capacity and data infrastructure.

CONCLUSIONS: Compared with osimertinib alone, osimertinib plus chemotherapy was likely to be cost-effective as first-line treatment for EGFR-mutated advanced NSCLC in China, but this cost-effectiveness was highly sensitive to the price of pemetrexed.

papers.abstract_en: The reasons why some patients with small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) benefit from chemotherapy and immunotherapy, while others rapidly develop resistance, are still undefined. Despite improved outcomes with platinum-based chemotherapy combined with immune checkpoint inhibitors have been correlated to activation of the innate immunity, the role of immune cells as potential markers of response is incompletely understood. Here, we characterized the transcriptional and functional landscape of circulating natural killer (NK) cells in patients with SCLC at baseline and after cisplatin treatment, stratified by clinical response. By integrating transcriptomics, cytokine profiling, and high-dimensional flow cytometry, we identified distinct NK cell subsets and developed an NK immune-fitness signature validated in independent intratumoral cohorts. At baseline, responders exhibited strong interferon signaling, enrichment of CD16+ cytotoxic NK1 cells, and enhanced activation, correlating with prolonged progression-free survival, whereas non-responders showed a quiescent NK3-dominant profile. Following treatment, responders displayed further expansion of cytotoxic NK1 cells, while non-responders shifted toward reduced functional capacity. Analyses of immune infiltrate confirmed CD16, but not CD56, as a predictor of improved survival. Integration of effector and evasion programs defined four immunological states, with the infiltrated-active phenotype associated with the most favorable outcomes. These findings show that both baseline NK cell fitness and therapy-induced remodelling may shape clinical response and identify CD16+ NK cells as a potential clinically actionable biomarker to guide patient stratification and also inform NK-targeted new therapeutic strategies.
